view.delete.what: forget a saved arrangement, deleting the file behind it

params.name: name
params.what: the saved view to remove; one that is not there is refused

view.delete.answers: The layout on screen is not touched: this removes the copy on disk, and nothing is asked first. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: drop a layout that is no longer used

view.list.what: name the saved arrangements there are to load, which is the only way to find out what a machine has kept
view.list.answers: The names alone, sorted, without the .json the files carry. Null where nothing has been saved, and null too where the platform cannot say where config lives, which reads the same from here. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: see which layouts this machine has kept

view.load.what: put a saved arrangement back, windows and all

params.name: name
params.what: the saved view, as view.list names it; one that is not there is refused

view.load.answers: It answers once the arrangement is asked for, the layouts and the view landing on the next frame and the windows opening after that. A file written before docking existed carries no layouts and loads as the declared presets rather than failing. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: go back to the layout a study is read in

view.save.what: keep the arrangement on screen under a name, so a layout built for one kind of work survives the next launch and the next machine

params.name: name
params.what: what to call it; an empty or missing name is refused, and a name already used is overwritten without asking

view.save.answers: It saves every view's arrangement, not only the one on screen, along with which view is showing and which panels are in windows of their own, to a file under the user's config directory. Refuses when no interface is attached.

example.what: keep the layout a coverage study is read in
